subject: Mutual action plan: POC environment and connectivity milestones
messages:
From: Sam Teller <sam.teller@mediq.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@mediq.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC MAP & environment ask (API keys, org, IP allowlist, peering)

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to lock down a Mutual Action Plan so our engineering team can get the POC environment up quickly. Two immediate asks from my side:

1) A concise checklist for setup items we need to complete on our side: org creation, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering windows.
2) A suggested close timeline (we're aiming for a 3-week evaluation starting the week of 6/21).

I've attached our procurement intake form (mediq-procurement.pdf) — procurement looped in on cc for any commercial questions.

High level questions:
- Do you provide ephemeral API keys or long-lived keys for the trial?
- What's the expected IP range footprint for VPC peering (so our VPC team can pre-approve)?
- Any required service accounts we should create in advance?

If you can send a one-page MAP and a technical preflight checklist, we'll get our infra team scheduled. Neha was recommended as the SE to work with — can you connect us?

Thanks,
Sam Teller
Director of Platform Engineering
MediQ Health
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>
To: Sam Teller <sam.teller@mediq.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.company>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.company>
Date: 2026-06-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC MAP & environment ask (API keys, org, IP allowlist, peering)

Sam —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a draft MAP (redwood-map-v1.xlsx) with milestones aligned to a 3-week eval starting 6/21. Quick answers inline, and looping in Neha for technical details and Marissa for onboarding/timeline coordination.

Quick answers:
- Keys: we can issue time-limited (ephemeral) API keys for the trial and optionally a scoped long-lived key for integration testing. Default recommendation: ephemeral keys for host-based calls + one service account key for CI (rotate after trial).
- IP footprint: our control plane uses a small set of egress IPs for API calls and the peering endpoints are per-region. Neha will attach the exact CIDR blocks and peering prerequisites.
- Service accounts: create a dedicated service account labeled mediq-redwood-poc with Owner on the test project (we'll scope down after initial tests).

Next steps I propose:
1) Tech sync (30-45m) this week to confirm CIDRs and peering windows.
2) We drop a MAP with milestones and acceptance criteria (I attached redwood-map-v1.xlsx).
3) Target: env up by 6/24, smoke tests 6/25–6/27, full eval 6/28–7/09, wrap and feedback 7/10.

Neha — can you post the network snippet and minimal sequence so Sam's infra can pre-approve?

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.company>
To: Sam Teller <sam.teller@mediq.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.company>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC MAP & environment ask (API keys, org, IP allowlist, peering)

Sam —

Thanks — attaching a concise network/config snippet (network-snippet.txt) and order-of-operations below. I'll keep this as the technical preflight we hand to infra teams.

Preflight checklist (minimal):
- Org & project: create a project named mediq-redwood-poc under your org. Grant one admin for the initial handoff.
- Service account: create mediq-redwood-poc-sa with roles: Compute Network Admin (for peering), Viewer for logging buckets, and IAM Service Account User.
- API keys: we will generate ephemeral API keys tied to the service account for server calls. If you need a CI key, create a k8s secret and we'll accept a one-time exchange token.
- IP allowlist: please allow the following CIDRs from your firewall for API callbacks: 52.23.128.0/26, 54.198.64.0/27 (US-west primary). If you are in another region tell me and I'll provide region-specific blocks.
- VPC peering: create a peering request from your VPC to redwood-poc-vpc-usw2. We'll need peering acceptance within the 2-hour window we schedule. Preferred windows: 6/24 09:00–11:00 or 6/24 15:00–17:00 PDT.
- DNS / routing: route 10.10.0.0/16 to our peered subnet (we recommend /24s for test nodes).
- Logs/retention: for trial, we keep 30 days of request logs; if you need longer retention let us know.

Sequence (recommended 48–72 hour setup path):
1) Day 0: Procurement ok + org/project and mediq-redwood-poc-sa created.
2) Day 1: Neha and your infra perform a peering window; we exchange ephemeral keys.
3) Day 2: Smoke tests against the test model (simple generate + KV cache validation).
4) Day 3+: Full eval.

Attachments: network-snippet.txt (contains CIDR list, peering endpoint ids, and a sample terraform snippet).

If you want, I can paste the terraform snippet inline in the sync. Otherwise I can walk your VPC owner through it on the call.

—Neha
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Ben / Neha —

Thanks — that checklist is exactly what our VPC team needs. Two follow-ups from procurement and infra:

- Procurement: we have a simple NDAs and a short SOW. Procurement asked if Redwood can accept our standard 45-day net term and if you require any additional insurance info. (procurement@mediq.com on cc)
- Infra: the VPC team asked if the CIDR blocks above are static for the trial or if they change. Also asked if there is any special routing required for egress to third-party telemetry endpoints.

We prefer the 6/24 09:00–11:00 peering window. Can you confirm a 30–45m tech sync on 6/16 or 6/17 to finalize details?

—Sam

MediQ Health
